matchup.raw_text: a Roman legionary vs a gorilla

mass_kg.note: No published body mass for Roman soldiers found for this fighter; category default (estimate 1 of 3, allowed by D-54).

source.title: Human height
source.quote: The Romans were slightly taller, with an average height of 169 cm (5 ft 7 in) for males and 158 cm (5 ft 2 in) for females.

size_m.note: Average height of Roman men generally, not soldiers specifically. Range is the standard +/-10%.

top_speed_mps.note: No published sprint speed for an armored soldier found for this fighter; category default (estimate 2 of 3, allowed by D-54).

source.title: Forces generated in stabbing attacks (Nolan, Hainsworth and Rutty 2017, Int. J. Legal Med. 132:229)
source.quote: for an unrestrained stab by a man, using their dominant hand, the mean peak force generated was approximately 150 N for pork thigh

attack_force_n.note: Stand-in for a gladius thrust: untrained volunteers stabbing with knives, not soldiers with swords. Range is +/-25%.

attacks_per_s.note: No published sword strike rate found for this fighter; category default (estimate 3 of 3, allowed by D-54).

source.title: Gladius
source.quote: Gladii that have been found measured 425–590 mm in length, 36–90 mm in width, and weighed between 1.2 and 1.6 kg.

reach_m.note: The sword's length, counted as reach (docs/research.md: a published weapon length counts). Upper figure of the found Mainz-type gladii (late 1st century BC to late 1st century AD); the source gives no mean.

armor_0_1.note: armor level 4: metal body armor and a large shield.

source.title: Gladiator
source.quote: most bouts would have lasted 10 to 15 minutes, or 20 minutes at most.

endurance_s.note: Stand-in: the length of a gladiator bout, a fighting duration (allowed by the PM on #29). Upper typical figure; low and high are the source's 10 and 20 minutes. Bout length for gladiators generally; heavily armed fighters tired faster, so this may overstate a legionary's stamina.

aggression_0_1.note: aggression level 4: trained soldier, confident against most opponents.

group_tactics_0_1.note: group tactics level 5: drilled unit acting as one (the rubric's own example).

source.title: Western lowland gorilla
source.quote: Males have an average weight of 140 kg (310 lb), females of 70 kg (150 lb).

mass_kg.note: Average adult male, from the lowland article; the Western gorilla article gives 145-191 kg for males, so this is the lower, lowland-specific figure. Range is the standard +/-10%.

source.title: Western gorilla
source.quote: Males average 1.67 m (5.5 ft) although reaching a height up to 1.76 m (5.8 ft)

size_m.note: Average standing height of adult males. High is the stated maximum in the same sentence; low is the standard -10%.

top_speed_mps.note: No published top speed found for this animal; category default.

source.title: 9 mammals, sharks, and reptiles with the strongest bite (IFAW)
source.quote: The bite force of the Western gorilla (Gorilla gorilla) was calculated by one study to be about 3,420 Newtons.
source.license: Publisher copyright, not an open license; one sentence cited

attack_force_n.note: Modeled maximum molar bite from Eng, Lieberman, Zink and Peters 2013, Am. J. Phys. Anthropol. 151:544 (doi:10.1002/ajpa.22296), as quoted by IFAW. Second-hand: the paper's PDF could not be opened. A molar, not canine, bite, so it is not directly comparable with the Wroe canine values on the wolf and grizzly sheets (593 N and 751 N); it is about 3 times the code's carnivore fit for 140 kg (1,016 N) and high for a fighting bite. Range is +/-50%, as on the elephant's stand-in.

attacks_per_s.note: No published attack rate found for this animal; category default.

armor_0_1.note: armor level 1: fur and bare skin.

source.title: Observations of severe and lethal coalitionary attacks in wild mountain gorillas (Rosenbaum, Vecellio and Stoinski 2016, Scientific Reports 6:37018)
source.quote: Approximately 3-4 minutes after the attack began, it abruptly stopped.

endurance_s.note: Stand-in, not a measured endurance: one 2004 attack by 26 mountain gorillas on a lone male, which the attackers stopped on their own after 3-4 minutes (the same paper reports another attack of 18 minutes). Used for an adult male western lowland gorilla. Upper end of the stated range; the source gives no mean.

aggression_0_1.note: aggression level 3: defends itself and its troop, avoids risky fights.

group_tactics_0_1.note: group tactics level 3: family troop that defends together.

result.deciding_factor_explainer: Strength decided it: Gorilla (3420 N) against Roman legionary (150 N).

fair_fight.message: A fair fight needs 48 Roman legionaries against 1 gorilla.

challenger.reason: African lion would be a slight underdog against Gorilla.
